# Testing the theory: is fatty tissue indistinguishable? {#sec-testing-the-theory}


If the theory is right, the breast comparison should work better for patients whose samples are water-rich (fibrous/glandular) than for patients whose
samples are fatty. To test this we take the rows of @fig-cohort (right), ordered by water peak height, and pick out the top 15% (the most
water-rich samples) and the bottom 15% (the fattiest). A patient is in a group if **any** of their samples falls in it. For the
patients in each group we then repeat the comparisons of @fig-all-patients exactly as before: each breast is still the mean of **all** of its scans,
not only the samples in the group, and each patient counts once.

**No patient is counted in both groups.** A patient can have one sample in the top 15% and another, from the same breast or the other one,
in the bottom 15%. Counting them in both would compare the same two breasts twice, once in each group, and since the comparison uses the
whole breast it would give the same answer both times, inflating whichever group it lands in. So a patient selected for the top group is left out of
the bottom group; here that removes 0
patients from the bottom group. The same rule applies to every top and bottom comparison below.

::: {#cell-fig-top-bottom .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
part_rows = {"top": by_water[:part_size], "bottom": by_water[-part_size:]}
part_results = {}  # part: {comparison: (patients whose first-named breast has the higher Water:Fat, patients compared, p-value)}
top_bottom_novas = top_and_bottom(*({ne.row_nova(names[k]) for k in part_rows[part]} for part in ("top", "bottom")))
for part, novas_here in top_bottom_novas.items():
    part_results[part] = {}
    for comparison, (base, others) in COMPARISONS.items():
        found = pairs(novas_here, base, others)
        higher = int(sum(other > base_ratio for base_ratio, other in found))
        part_results[part][comparison] = (higher, len(found), binomtest(higher, len(found)).pvalue if found else np.nan)

def result_text(part, comparison):
    """A group's result for the text, such as "9/11 (82%)"."""
    higher, total, _ = part_results[part][comparison]
    return f"{higher}/{total} ({higher / total:.0%})" if total else "no patients"

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7  # small text so both panels fit side by side on an A4 page
fig, (map_ax, bar_ax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 4))
for ax in (map_ax, bar_ax):
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)  # square panels
ordered = rows[by_water]
covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(ordered).all(axis=0))
columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
low, high = np.nanpercentile(ordered[:, columns], (1, 99))
left, right = q[columns][[0, -1]]
map_ax.imshow(ordered[:, columns], aspect="auto", cmap=cmap, vmin=low, vmax=high, interpolation="nearest",
              extent=(left, right, len(ordered), 0))
# dim the middle rows, and outline the top and bottom 15%
map_ax.axhspan(part_size, len(ordered) - part_size, color="white", alpha=0.55, lw=0)
for (start, stop), colour, text in (((0, part_size), TOP_COLOUR, f"top {PART}%: water-rich"),
                                    ((len(ordered) - part_size, len(ordered)), BOTTOM_COLOUR, f"bottom {PART}%: fatty")):
    map_ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((2, start), right - 2, stop - start, fill=False, edgecolor=colour, lw=2.5, clip_on=False))
    map_ax.text(right - 0.4, (start + stop) / 2, text, color="white", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7, fontweight="bold")
map_ax.axvline(14, color="white", ls="--", lw=0.8)
map_ax.set(xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, right), yticks=[])
map_ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])
map_ax.annotate("", xy=(-0.11, 0.9), xytext=(-0.11, 0.1), xycoords="axes fraction",
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color="black", lw=1.2), annotation_clip=False)
map_ax.text(-0.11, 0.07, "Fatty", transform=map_ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="top")
map_ax.text(-0.11, 0.93, "Fibrous/\nGlandular", transform=map_ax.transAxes, ha="center", va="bottom")

width = 0.38
for k, comparison in enumerate(COMPARISONS):
    for offset, part, colour in ((-width / 2, "top", TOP_COLOUR), (width / 2, "bottom", BOTTOM_COLOUR)):
        higher, total, p_value = part_results[part][comparison]
        if not total:
            continue
        bar_ax.bar(k + offset, 100 * higher / total, width=width, color=colour, label=f"{part} {PART}%" if k == 0 else None)
        bar_ax.text(k + offset, 100 * higher / total + 2, f"{higher}/{total}\np={p_value:.2g}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=5)
bar_ax.axhline(50, color="black", ls=":", lw=1)
bar_ax.text(len(COMPARISONS) - 0.5, 51, "chance", ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=6)
bar_ax.set(xticks=range(len(COMPARISONS)), ylim=(0, 110), yticks=range(0, 101, 20),
           ylabel="patients whose first-named breast\nhas the higher Water:Fat (%)")
bar_ax.set_xticklabels([c.replace(" vs ", "\nvs ") for c in COMPARISONS], fontsize=6)
bar_ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
bar_ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", ncols=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

::: {.callout-note title="What the top/bottom selection appears to show"}
CANCER vs NORMAL: in the water-rich top **8/8 \(100%\)** of patients have the higher Water:Fat in the CANCER breast,
against **3/7 \(43%\)** in the fatty bottom. The comparison works best where the beam samples fibrous/glandular tissue.
:::

For CANCER vs NORMAL and BENIGN vs NORMAL the **water-rich top does better than the fatty bottom**, as the theory predicts:

| Comparison | Top 15% (water-rich) | Bottom 15% (fatty) |
|---|---|---|
| CANCER vs NORMAL | **8/8 \(100%\)**, p = 0\.0078 | **3/7 \(43%\)** |
| BENIGN vs NORMAL | **5/7 \(71%\)** | **3/9 \(33%\)** |
| CANCER vs BENIGN | **0/3 \(0%\)** | **7/8 \(88%\)** |

In the fatty bottom the comparisons against NORMAL are **at or below chance**, while in the water-rich top the CANCER vs NORMAL result is the strongest
in the report (p = 0\.0078).

CANCER vs BENIGN goes the other way, but only **3 patients** in the top have one CANCER and one
BENIGN breast, too few to say anything.

Taken at face value this is a strong result. But it is not a fair test, as the next section explains.

## Why this is cheating

@fig-top-bottom looks back at data we already have and picks out the samples that suit the analysis. Two things make it unfair.

1. **It is retrospective.** The groups were chosen after the measurements, by looking at the very signal we then analyse; and the 15% cut-off, and
   using non-normal rows, were settled after trying other choices on the same data.
2. **The selection favours one breast.** A patient joins the water-rich top through a water-rich *CANCER* (or BENIGN) sample. That sample is part of its
   breast's mean, so it raises that breast's Water:Fat and makes it more likely to come out higher. In the fatty bottom it works the other way, which
   is why the contrast in @fig-top-bottom is so large.

The second point can be shown directly. @fig-normal-rows repeats @fig-top-bottom, but chooses the patients by their **NORMAL** breast instead: the rows are
every NORMAL sample, ordered by water peak height. Everything else is the same: each breast is the mean of all its scans, each patient counts once,
and a patient in the top group is left out of the bottom one.

::: {#cell-fig-normal-rows .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
normal_novas, normal_rows, normal_names, _, _ = ne.sample_view(by_label["NORMAL"])
in_range = (normal_novas >= NOVA_RANGE[0]) & (normal_novas <= NOVA_RANGE[1])
normal_rows, normal_names = normal_rows[in_range], [n for n, keep in zip(normal_names, in_range) if keep]
with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
    normal_water = np.nanmean(normal_rows[:, (q >= WATER[0]) & (q <= WATER[1])], axis=1)
normal_order = np.argsort(-normal_water, kind="stable")  # highest water peak first
normal_size = round(len(normal_order) * PART / 100)
normal_groups = top_and_bottom({ne.row_nova(normal_names[k]) for k in normal_order[:normal_size]},
                               {ne.row_nova(normal_names[k]) for k in normal_order[-normal_size:]})
NORMAL_COMPARISONS = [c for c, (base, _) in COMPARISONS.items() if base == "NORMAL"]
normal_results = {}
for part, novas_here in normal_groups.items():
    normal_results[part] = {}
    for comparison in NORMAL_COMPARISONS:
        base, others = COMPARISONS[comparison]
        found = pairs(novas_here, base, others)
        higher = int(sum(other > base_ratio for base_ratio, other in found))
        normal_results[part][comparison] = (higher, len(found), binomtest(higher, len(found)).pvalue if found else np.nan)

def normal_text(part, comparison):
    higher, total, _ = normal_results[part][comparison]
    return f"{higher}/{total} ({higher / total:.0%})" if total else "no patients"

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7  # small text so both panels fit side by side on an A4 page
fig, (map_ax, bar_ax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 4))
for ax in (map_ax, bar_ax):
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)  # square panels
ordered_normal = normal_rows[normal_order]
n_covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(ordered_normal).all(axis=0))
n_columns = slice(n_covered[0], n_covered[-1] + 1)
n_low, n_high = np.nanpercentile(ordered_normal[:, n_columns], (1, 99))
n_left, n_right = q[n_columns][[0, -1]]
map_ax.imshow(ordered_normal[:, n_columns], aspect="auto", cmap=cmap, vmin=n_low, vmax=n_high, interpolation="nearest",
              extent=(n_left, n_right, len(ordered_normal), 0))
map_ax.axhspan(normal_size, len(ordered_normal) - normal_size, color="white", alpha=0.55, lw=0)
for (start, stop), colour, text in (((0, normal_size), TOP_COLOUR, f"top {PART}%: water-rich"),
                                    ((len(ordered_normal) - normal_size, len(ordered_normal)), BOTTOM_COLOUR, f"bottom {PART}%: fatty")):
    map_ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((2, start), n_right - 2, stop - start, fill=False, edgecolor=colour, lw=2.5, clip_on=False))
    map_ax.text(n_right - 0.4, (start + stop) / 2, text, color="white", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7, fontweight="bold")
map_ax.axvline(14, color="white", ls="--", lw=0.8)
map_ax.set(xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, n_right), yticks=[], ylabel=f"{len(ordered_normal)} NORMAL samples, by water peak height")
map_ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])

width = 0.38
for k, comparison in enumerate(NORMAL_COMPARISONS):
    for offset, part, colour in ((-width / 2, "top", TOP_COLOUR), (width / 2, "bottom", BOTTOM_COLOUR)):
        higher, total, p_value = normal_results[part][comparison]
        if not total:
            continue
        bar_ax.bar(k + offset, 100 * higher / total, width=width, color=colour, label=f"{part} {PART}%" if k == 0 else None)
        bar_ax.text(k + offset, 100 * higher / total + 2, f"{higher}/{total}\np={p_value:.2g}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=5)
bar_ax.axhline(50, color="black", ls=":", lw=1)
bar_ax.text(len(NORMAL_COMPARISONS) - 0.5, 51, "chance ", ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=6)
bar_ax.set(xticks=range(len(NORMAL_COMPARISONS)), ylim=(0, 115), yticks=range(0, 101, 20),
           ylabel="patients whose first-named breast\nhas the higher Water:Fat (%)")
bar_ax.set_xticklabels([c.replace(" vs ", "\nvs ") for c in NORMAL_COMPARISONS], fontsize=6)
bar_ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
bar_ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.14), ncols=2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

![**Left**: every NORMAL sample from Nova 250 onwards, ordered by water peak height, with the water-rich top 15% (blue) and the fatty bottom 15% (yellow) picked out. **Right**: for the patients with a NORMAL sample in each group, the share whose first-named breast has the higher Water:Fat, with the number of patients and the two-sided binomial p-value against 50%.](fatty_test_files/figure-html/fig-normal-rows-output-1.png){#fig-normal-rows width=752 height=403}
:::
:::


| Chosen by the NORMAL breast | Top 15% (water-rich) | Bottom 15% (fatty) |
|---|---|---|
| CANCER vs NORMAL | **4/7 \(57%\)**, p = 1 | **5/6 \(83%\)**, p = 0\.22 |
| BENIGN vs NORMAL | **3/11 \(27%\)** | **3/4 \(75%\)** |

::: {.callout-important title="Key result: the outcome follows the breast used for selection"}
Chosen by the NORMAL breast, @fig-top-bottom reverses. Where the NORMAL breast was sampled in glandular tissue, the CANCER breast has the higher Water:Fat in
only **4/7 \(57%\)** of patients; where it was sampled in fat, in **5/6 \(83%\)**.
So the result of @fig-top-bottom follows whichever breast decided the selection, not whether the tissue is glandular: a breast's Water:Fat depends strongly on
where its samples happened to be taken. Looking back and choosing samples this way cannot tell us whether glandular samples classify better.
:::
